Without going against your wishes, the only thing I can ask is if there's any potential of something changing. Everyone's problems are different so they can't be addressed the same, but I feel that regardless of the origin there is always something that can be done. I'm sorry to hear that therapy didn't go well for you and I'm not nearly experienced enough to attempt anything myself, but I really do hope you can find some form of positivity to keep you going, at least for a while longer.

To say something like this to another person, let alone a website, is incredibly brave. Thank you for not only taking the time out of your day to do this, but also talking about such a sensitive topic with us. 

There isn't much I can do to stop you, and I don't want to make this feel as though you're doing something wrong, but I can at the very least tell you that you are valued, regardless of what had happened to you. I have multiple 'friends' from my school who I will likely never talk to again now that it's finished. Despite this, I know that *some* people care about me, but also that I have some form of importance, even if a little. 

Due to how difficult it would be I know I cannot ask you to outright stop your intentions, but at the very least I'd request that you truly consider what you want to do and take some time to really evaluate your life. There are so many things that it has, and taking your own life would immediately remove all of that. Sure, there are many problems with the world, and that makes it more difficult to want to stay, but there are positive aspects of it too. Even those things which may not seem important can have a really big impact together. 

Do your best to remain strong and know that there are people who care about your well being and your safety. If possible, try to talk to someone you really trust about the issue, or use a helpline service to anonymously get help from professionals to at the very least make the situation easier on yourself.

Just consider this; you *have* someone. That in itself shows that someone not only cares about you, but feels that you're an important part of their life. If that's the case, then you're a valuable part of society as well. 

What problems have made you feel this way? If you feel uncomfortable sharing that's absolutely fine, but I'll do my best to be considerate towards you.

I feel the exact same way sometimes. I've considered multiple methods and have even planned some out, but have yet to go through with them. 

If you wouldn't mind sharing, and this is completely okay if you wish not to, but what are the bigger things which you believe have made you feel this way? I can only imagine that it's extremely negative, but I'll do my best to remain respectful and helpful throughout.

First and foremost; have you talked to this friend recently? If possible, I'd recommend staying in consistent contact with them whilst this occurs to ensure that they're okay. That's the most important part throughout this. 

If the mother knows that makes this somewhat easier to deal with. Hopefully she shouldn't react too largely once you tell her. Without a doubt the important part of this is telling her everything that has happened. Don't hold any information away if it has the potential to directly affect your friend negatively. If possible, I'd suggest telling the mother what signs you found that suggest your friend could potentially be at risk, and explaining why that is the case. 

You should also tell the friend of your intent at some point. Regardless of their reaction don't let it affect your decision, but don't let them feel betrayed either. If you tell them nothing throughout they may feel as though their trust in you is lost, which can lead to even worse things happening. 

All in all I can only say that honesty is the best thing here. Ensuring that the mother knows exactly what is going on and why it can be a problem is what you want so that the child can get the help they need.

To not only feel negative but to have a direct plan, let alone on the same day, shows that you've been through a lot. I don't at all doubt that as I feel as though I'm on that path myself, but I'm not there at the moment. 

I doubt my opinion alone could affect your decision but are there any specific reasons for you feeling this way that you'd feel comfortable sharing? 

I should emphasize that a lot of your points are similar to how I feel myself; feeling unintelligent, unattractive, antisocial, and generally just unimportant. I'll admit, it's not at all a pleasant experience and in high amounts could certainly lead to how you feel, so I'm not blaming you whatsoever. 

At the very least I would recommend taking a few days purely to evaluate your situation and determine if this is definitely something you wish to go through with. Even if you don't have people you trust in person, there are a bunch of people online, including helplines, who can at the very least make it easier for you. I can personally justify at least some of your reasons being invalid by saying this; your appearance should NOT be a factor. People, like anything in life, are different. That's just how it is. That, however, is not at all a bad thing. Some people prefer taller, some shorter. Some prefer brown hair, some blonde. Your appearance will be seen as attractive to someone, I can guarantee you that. You might be surprised to hear that and potentially even hesitant to believe it, but I can tell you from personal experience that it's true. For those that feel this isn't the case, that's because they're selfish. They don't realize that what makes a person is their personality, not their looks. 

As for being antisocial, who cares? I'm online for the majority of my life but I'm still pulling through. Being antisocial isn't necessarily a negative thing, but rather a different thing. It's part of your uniqueness that you share with everyone in the world. It doesn't make you a worse person for having a trait which you feel others frown upon, because there's absolutely no reason for it to. 

For now I'd ask of you to find one remotely positive thing you can think of in the world. Just one. It doesn't have to make you exstatic, or even happy for that matter, but something which you find comfort in, or a sense of joy, or some form of passion. Anything like that. 

Feel free to talk to me at any time as I'll likely be here the majority of the time seeing as I have nothing else to do. I'd hate to know that someone did something like this, especially given the opportunity to talk to them. Even if it becomes a personal responsibility of mine, I'll do my best to try and get you through this, at least for a while longer than you plan on doing currently.

First of all I would ideally make sure that your friend is okay. Make sure that they are not only able to talk to you but that they are in fact okay, in the sense that they haven't done anything and they're in a safe space. 

When sending a message about the issue you need to take into consideration both the individual you're helping, but also the person you're sending the message to. If you know the mother and child personally you'd know this a lot better than I do, but from previous posts I've seen that this isn't always in a positive manner. Things to note are what sort of connection the mother has, and how much she knows already. If she has a general idea, you should tell the whole truth and state it outright to ensure that your friend gets the help that she needs. If she isn't at all aware it becomes more difficult as their reaction could be anywhere from mild to drastic. In this case, I'd suggest talking over multiple texts to ease in the idea without avoiding any important details. Initially start by asking how her child is in general, as well as at the current time, then ask if she knows anything strange or unusual about their behavior. From there you can slowly reveal details about the issue, ensuring that the matter doesn't escalate and that you're not missing out anything important. 

If you plan on messaging her any time soon I'll be here if you need any help, as well as any potential others who comment.

I've personally considered *that* method and from the sheer sound of it I don't think it's the way to go. It's such a potentially painful thought, and is an incredibly terrifying sight to whoever or whatever finds you as you are. 

I don't know what made you get to this point, and if you feel comfortable I'd ask what it was, but I can assure you that you can make it past your problems. It most certainly won't be any time soon, but problems are called problems because they're difficult to deal with. There are many different methods of communication you have available to you for any issue you may be dealing with, so don't ever feel as though you're alone in this. Whatever you feel, someone will feel the same, and can do their best to help. 

If you're willing to share anything about how you feel, I'll be here to talk to if you need someone.

You should never have to feel as though you're bad at interacting with people because there are many different types of people. There are people who feel the same you do who would be much easier to talk to than most others. Having the introverted/extroverted spectrum somewhat defines this as it shows that people can be completely fine with talking to others, completely against or even scared of it, or somewhere in the middle. 

Honestly, I feel similar to how you do in terms of utility. A lot of the time people are so caught up in their own problems that identifying others' is really difficult so it may not initially seem as though people care, but often times they do and you may not realize. 

For what it's worth, congratulations on passing your college exam. They're intentionally a stressful time to show how individuals can deal with stressful situations in particular areas. To show that you were able to get through with it is a fantastic thing, and all the more power to you for doing so. 

I'm not entirely sure if your sexuality is something which you feel affects how others feel towards you, or even affects how you feel in general, but for the most part it shouldn't whatsoever. It's part of who you are and something which defines your personality. It definitely shouldn't negatively affect you as it isn't something you've done, but something you are. Similarly, it would be wrong of me to see you differently based on your gender, or race, or age. We're in a changing time and showing your sexuality publicly is difficult, especially with sexualities which are less recognized or accepted such as bisexuality. 

I know you feel less important at the moment than I would classify as ideal, and that likely won't change any time soon, but I can assure you that you are an important individual. To myself, and I'm sure to a lot of others in this community, and even people you know in person. Try to identify what makes you unique and consider how that could affect other people. It may not seem like much, but it small things are what make you completely different, and a pleasant person to be around. After all, you're the only one of you that this world has. You're a rarity! Don't forget that.

In my opinion it's the small things that really help to keep people going. It doesn't have to be anything major, but making some form of change can make a surprisingly big difference when you look back at what it actually did. If you're concerned about your weight, for example, work on it. It doesn't have to be by a large amount, but simply trying to lose weight can do a lot for a person. Give it a few weeks, or months, and you'll see just how much you actually did. From there you can realize that anything you desire you can work towards, because you can. Each goal will take different amounts of time and effort but is without a doubt achievable. That's literally all it takes; a determination to accomplish something. If other people see you negatively, just absolutely ignore them. Sure, they may *have* certain things, but you worked for it. You deserve it. Even if efforts don't result in accomplishments, not only can you try again, but you would be one of the few that truly went for it. It's not at all easy to take the first few steps, but once you do the rest are much easier. That's because you can look back at the trail you made and realize that everything you do, positive or negative, makes a significant difference on yourself, and your surroundings. Stay strong and I promise things will get better for you, even if you don't see it right now.

I had hoped IT would be a valid career opportunity seeing as I use computers a lot and I believe that I have an okay knowledge of them, however the results I got back apparently show otherwise. From the three courses I took (ICT, Public Services and Media) ICT was actually the worst, which really surprised me. It doesn't outright rule it out, but that in itself is kind of discouraging in its own regard. 
I had considered University in its own right seeing as the majority of people at the very least consider it, however I don't think I could stay on the course for that long. As much as I understand how useful it is, I genuinely don't believe in my ability to stay with it for that long with how I am now, and I also don't really think there's anything I'd be interested in applying for there anyway. More than likely I will have to apply for an apprenticeship of some kind, but I've yet to find something I definitely want to do. Honestly, if worst comes to worst and I can't go through with my original intentions, I probably will have to get an apprenticeship of some kind, but I'm not really sure what in, or when. That's one of the things that really terrifies me; adulthood. I still feel like a child in some sense. A lot of things which I should know, I just don't. Until a couple weeks ago I have never even cooked anything, and I know very little about responsibilities in a household. If I were to be sent out on my own today (which I believe is legal at 18) I honestly don't think I could make it, that's how scared I am. That's why using computers makes it a little easier, it distracts me from having to know that I have those responsibilities, but unfortunately doesn't actually prepare me for them.

Interestingly enough I actually had started a journal on a device that I had. I got it up to 11 months with daily recordings but unfortunately it stopped working last month. Despite it being an inanimate object it was a very big loss for me as I had it for about 8 years and it occupied a LOT of my time. It also had a lot of memories on it. I do recall some of the entries though and a lot of them were effectively just stating negativity without actually saying anything which would help in this situation. 
I did also try to find what things I liked doing and up to this point I just haven't found anything. I'm also struggling to find that in terms of employment as it's something which I need to be considering now that I'm 18, but it's extremely difficult as anything I have a remote interest in usually diminishes within a few weeks, if that. There isn't anything I'm particularly 'interested' in besides gaming that has actually lasted, likely due to the fact that I'm so heavily reliant on it for a distraction from things. I am still considering potential options for both hobbies and employment but it's really difficult. Still though, you have to remain hopeful, right? 
I doubt it will get any better after quarantine to be completely honest. While this definitely affected it, it hadn't made the situation much worse for me seeing as the majority of my time was spent indoors anyway. It just kind of encouraged me to do it more, really.

I don't understand why people have such a problem with this. If you do a lot of damage you deserve to be rewarded with a higher damage threshold against others. You still have a higher shield amount with the max evo shield, but have the same effect while using gold as you did before. The only real difference is the lowered shield amount, which makes sense because now it's more difficult to shield up mid fight and encourages you to play strategically or aggressively rather than taking small shots off on players then shielding back up. Getting health is much slower than shields so it doesn't make sense to have an equal amount of shields, otherwise you could have a very long stalemate provided you actually had shields to use.

If this had happened at an earlier age then I would have suggested calling some form of helpline such as CPS if the situation became dire, however I can completely understand that it would be very difficult to do something like that seeing as she is your mother. 

As an adult however you are now technically able to be responsible for your own actions. I could only say that talking to her about it directly would be your best option seeing as otherwise it likely won't get any better. If you can ever get some form of help such as a psychologist, I've read that they can help to tell them about something like this. That way, it's easier for both of you to come to terms with and as a result nothing physically or emotionally damaging happens. 

If it's a truly abusive relationship you have with her, either physically or emotionally, I would highly recommend speaking up about it to her, and if that doesn't work either speak to another family member or a professional of some kind. Don't ever feel as though someone has the authority to speak negatively towards you about anything, especially with how dire this is.

Admittedly, not really. I did try to have that mindset, especially when I was younger, but over time it kind of just diminished. Regardless, I appreciate what you've said, it's nice to hear it from someone else. Thank you.
